topics: What audit logs capture (admin actions, API keys, role changes)
Retention defaults vs extended retention and export
Encryption and KMS: CMEK vs Redwood-managed
RBAC for log access, SSO/SAML integration
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Well run through audit logs and admin activity today. Hopefully not too heavy but we want to make sure you have what you need for compliance.
[00:12] Lisa Carter (Omega CISO): Thanks, Jordan. Were particularly concerned about who can see logs and the retention. SOC 2 auditors asked for examples.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood SE): Great, well cover capture surface, export options, encryption, and RBAC. Quick call intro: Jordan and I from Redwood, Marcus on infra docs -- sorry Marcus is on but muted.
[00:33] Tom (Omega Infra): Morning, thanks. We run in AWS, want exports to our central security S3 and Splunk. Also concerned with PII in logs.
[00:45] Priya: Understood. At a high level, Redwood audit logs capture admin API calls, console logins, role/permission changes, model deploys, model/version rollouts, key rotations, and export events. We also log token and API key creations and deletions, but not full user prompt content unless customer opts in for debug logs.
[01:10] Lisa: When you say "console logins", is that SSO only or do you store local creds if someone used a password?
[01:16] Jordan: By default customers enable SSO via SAML/Okta, and we recommend that. If local creds are used we capture the event (login success/fail) but not the credential.
[01:28] Rahul (Omega Compliance): Do logs include the actual prompts or generated completions?
[01:33] Priya: Good question. No, we do not include prompt/completion content in admin audit logs. We have separate request/response logs for usage which are controlled by retention settings and opt-in. Admin/audit logs focus on metadata: who, what, when, IP, request id, resource id, and change diff if applicable (eg role changed from X to Y).
[01:55] Tom: How granular are the diffs? Do you show the entire JSON change or just a high level note?
[02:02] Priya: We generally store the before/after snapshot for role and config changes — we call it a change delta. For big config objects we store the key fields; sometimes the transcriber (note: autos transcribed doc) might say K-V cash instead of KV cache, sorry.
[02:20] Lisa: Can we export logs to our S3 bucket and have them land encrypted with our KMS?
[02:25] Marcus (Redwood): Yes — we support multiple export sinks. We can push daily or near-real-time events to S3, BigQuery, or send to Splunk via HTTP Event Collector. For S3 we support SSE-S3, SSE-KMS using your AWS KMS CMK (CMEK), or Redwood-managed KMS. If you provide a CMK we encrypt at rest with your key and we never hold key material.
[02:52] Rahul: What about retention? Auditors want 1 year of admin logs and 7 years of some evidence. What are defaults?
[03:00] Priya: Default retention for audit logs is 90 days in the console and searchable via the Redwood Console. We offer extended retention add-ons: 1 year, 3 years, or custom terms (enterprise contract) where logs are kept in our managed store or exported to your storage for longer retention.
[03:18] Lisa: If we export to our bucket, does Redwood keep a copy in the managed store?
[03:23] Jordan: By default we keep the 90 days. Exports are a copy; if you want us to purge earlier we can set policies, but typical pattern is keep 90 days in Redwood and push a separate archive to customer S3 for longer retention.
[03:38] Tom: What about SIEM mapping? Splunk expects certain field names.
[03:42] Marcus: We provide a sample schema and recommended field mappings for Splunk and Datadog. We'll send a CSV/JSON mapping and an example exported file. For Splunk we have an HEC-compatible delivery option so events map in near real time.
[03:56] Lisa: Auditors also want to know who can view audit trails. How do you control access?
[04:03] Priya: Access to audit logs is controlled via RBAC. We have roles: Org Admin, Security Auditor (read-only to logs, no ability to change settings), DevOps (limited to infra logs), and Support (redacted view). Organizations can map SAML groups to these roles. Only Org Admin or Security Auditor with explicit permission can download raw exported logs.
[04:33] Rahul: Can you redact PII before export?
[04:37] Jordan: We provide configurable redaction for common PII patterns (emails, credit-card-like numbers). For more advanced PII redaction we can run a POC to apply custom regex or a redaction pipeline in the export path (e.g., Lambda) — that would be part of the POC.
[04:55] Tom: Does exporting to BigQuery keep the schema? We want to run queries across logs and usage.
[04:59] Marcus: Yes — BigQuery export uses a flattened table schema we include in the doc. Queryable fields include timestamp, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, diff_before, diff_after, source_ip, user_agent, request_id, region. We’ll send that schema.
[05:22] Lisa: About encryption in transit?
[05:24] Priya: All exports use TLS 1.2+ in transit. For pushing to S3 we use signed PutObject; for Splunk HEC we use TLS and token authentication. For BigQuery we use GCP service account credentials to write directly.
[05:41] Rahul: Wanted to confirm: if we provide a CMEK, do you rotate or manage it?
[05:46] Jordan: We never manage your CMK. You control rotation policies in AWS. Redwood stores only the key alias and uses KMS APIs to encrypt; we do not store plaintext.
[05:57] Tom: Are audit logs included in SOC 2 package?
[06:00] Marcus: Yes, audit logging and admin activity are part of our SOC 2 scope. We can provide sample logs and the SOC 2 report. Note there may be redactions in the sample.
[06:12] Lisa: How do you maintain immutability or tamper evidence?
[06:17] Priya: For managed storage we provide write-once append-only storage with HMACs and retention locks for the contract terms. For customer S3 exports you can enable S3 object lock with legal hold to ensure immutability. We also support push to an external SIEM where you can enable your own immutability controls.
[06:36] Tom: If an admin deletes a role, is that action captured and can we reconstruct who did it and when?
[06:42] Priya: Yes — deletion events are captured with before snapshot, actor id, request id, and timestamp. That’s part of the standard audit event.
[06:52] Lisa: Any limits on storage throughput for exports?
[06:55] Marcus: Not for normal customers; for very high event volume we recommend batching or near-real-time streaming to a Kinesis or PubSub via our integration. For S3 we do daily bundles or streaming per-event writes depending on your preference. Pricing differs for high throughput.
[07:14] Rahul: Ok this is great. Can we see an example export with redaction applied?
[07:18] Jordan: Yes, action item; Priya will provision an S3 bucket and we’ll run a short POC and provide sample files.
[07:26] Priya: I’ll also attach the runbook for configuring CMEK, SAML mapping, and the retention tiers.
[07:34] Tom: A couple practical questions: who in Redwood has access to raw logs for support escalations?
[07:39] Marcus: We have limited support roles. Support access is logged and requires an access justification. Access is short-lived and requires Org Admin approval. We also have an internal audit trail showing who viewed the logs with timestamp and reason.
[07:57] Lisa: If we need seven years, how do we handle storage costs?
[08:01] Jordan: Two patterns: 1) export to your S3 and store in Glacier/Archive; 2) contract extended retention with Redwood where we store cold archives for a fee. Typically customers prefer option 1 for long-term retention.
[08:16] Tom: For the SOC 2 evidence we’ll need a sample of the audit logs showing role changes around the time of last audit. Can you produce that?
[08:22] Marcus: Yes — we can provide time-bounded exports. We'll redact sensitive fields as needed.
[08:29] Rahul: Are there any gotchas around GDPR or data residency?
[08:33] Priya: Audit logs are regionally stored based on your org region. For EU customers we keep managed logs in EU regions. Exports to customer buckets should respect your residency controls — if you export to US S3 that's your choice but we'll flag it for compliance.
[08:51] Lisa: Ok good. Anything else we should know about log format changes across product versions?
[08:55] Jordan: We version the log schema. We provide a schema version in the event header and maintain backward compatibility for 18 months, with advance notices for breaking changes.
[09:07] Tom: How do we integrate the audit logs with our ticketing system?
[09:10] Priya: We can push events via webhook to your ticketing system or to an event queue. We also support pushing aggregated alerts into Slack or PagerDuty.
[09:23] Lisa: Great. I think we have enough to start. Can you recap the deliverables?
[09:27] Jordan: Sure — Jordan will send the runbook & retention pricing, Priya will provision S3 export and produce sample files with redaction enabled, Marcus will share schema and SIEM mappings, and we’ll schedule a follow-up to review exported files and mapping.
[09:44] Rahul: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:47] Jordan: Thanks all, we’ll follow up by Friday with runbook and dates for the POC.
[09:54] [END OF TRANSCRIPT]
